title: Autonomous safe rollback & state reconciler for config-driven cost optimizations
creator: Priya Patel
description: Build an automatic rollback and state-reconciliation subsystem that safely applies suggested batching/caching configuration changes (from Redwood Optimize) and can automatically roll back or reconcile runtime state when guardrails are breached. The subsystem must support multiple trigger sources (recommendation engine, manual rollout, scheduled jobs), evaluate guardrails (latency SLO, error-rate, cost-per-token delta, quality regression signals), and perform safe state transitions with minimal disruption. It must also continuously reconcile desired config (what was applied) with observed runtime state and repair drift or undo changes when needed.
acceptance_criteria: Can apply a config change via API and record a verifiable immutable change event (config hash + metadata).

Automatic rollback triggers fire when any configured guardrail is exceeded for the configured evaluation window (example thresholds: latency > 2x baseline P95, error-rate +1.5%, cost-per-token increase > 10%).
Rollback action can be performed automatically without data loss or, when unsafe, will produce an automated stall and human alert.
Reconciler detects drift between desired config and actual runtime state within 60s of drift and performs a safe re-apply or rollback.
System provides an audit trail (who/what/why/timestamp), and integrates with Console for per-change telemetry and a single-click manual rollback.
Chaos/rollout tests show no more than 1% increase in request failures during rollouts and rollbacks in staging.
design_notes: Event-sourced change log: every config apply produces an append-only change event with desired state, applied-at, actor, canary percent, and target model-pool. Use content-addressed hash to validate integrity.
Trigger types: metric-sourced (datadog/observability), recommendation-sourced (Optimize), manual API, scheduled job. Each trigger includes metadata and a TTL to avoid repeated stale actions.

Guardrails: multilayer checks including SLO checks (latency/error), cost deltas computed against rolling baseline, quality regressions detected by eval-set scoring, and internal health signals (OOM, GPU queue length).

Canary rollout model: gradual traffic shift by routing percentage (0 -> target) with evaluation windows and automatic hold/rollback. Canary uses shadow runs for cost-unblocked metrics where appropriate.

Reconciler design: leader-elected controller per-region polling actual worker state (config version, kernel flags, batching policy, cache state). Reconciler compares desired config hash and runtime probes; actions are idempotent.

State operations: safe-apply must be transactional where possible: (1) stage config to workers, (2) validate stage via probes (smoke latency and correctness), (3) flip traffic, (4) verify post-flip metrics. Rollback reverses steps and uses last-known-good snapshot.
success_metrics: % of automatic rollbacks that required no manual intervention >= 90%
Mean time to detect/rollback (MTTR) for guardrail breaches < 3 minutes
False positive rollback rate < 2% in staging
Overall platform cost delta attributable to automated batching/caching changes >= 12% in first 90 days
No customer-facing incidents attributable to automated rollbacks in prod for first 6 months
rollout_plan: Phase 0: run reconciler in read-only detection mode in staging for 2 weeks to collect drift signals and tune probes.
Phase 1: enable apply with canary traffic 1% in staging; simulate guardrail breaches via fault-injection (latency, error spikes, cost anomalies).
Phase 2: limited prod pilot for non-critical tenants with manual approval; strict alerting to SRE and PM on any rollback event.
Phase 3: enable automated rollback in prod for customer tier 'trial' and 'dev' with conservative thresholds; iterative expansion over 6 weeks.
Phase 4: full enablement for hosted and dedicated when telemetry validates low false-positive rate and reconcile latency meets SLA.
risks: Over-eager automatic rollback may oscillate configuration causing thrashing if thresholds are not damped (use hysteresis and minimum evaluation windows).
Inconsistent rollback across heterogeneous pools (different kernel/quantization) could leave fleets partially degraded; reconciler must be aware of model-variant compatibility tables.

Stateful caches (KV/prefix) require careful migration semantics: immediate rollback might invalidate caches and spike downstream latency/cost. Use staged cache invalidation and backfill where possible.
Incorrect metric baselines could cause false rollbacks; need robust anomaly detection and baseline refresh cadence.

2026-02-20: Prototyped change-event schema and stored it in event-store; basic apply API scaffold created. (Ethan)
2026-02-28: Design review held with PM and SRE. Feedback: add forced-stall mode for safety and explicit human override UI in Console. (Design feedback incorporated).
2026-03-05: Reconciler read-only runner deployed to staging; collected 48h of drift data. Found frequent transient drift during autoscaler fluctuations — added 30s stabilization window. (Ethan)
2026-03-10: Integration with Optimize recommendations prepared; first end-to-end dry-run succeeded in staging without triggering guardrail violations. QA to run fault-injection next. (Priya)
2026-03-12: Implemented canary percent gating and added audit event linkage to Console change log. Next: PR for rollback orchestration and test harness.
